_about: The one copy of every rule number. Read by sim/rules.py (the Python simulator)
and web/js/engine.js (the browser table and JS bots); neither holds its own.
Names are camelCase; Python uses the snake_case form of the same name
(startingPurse -> starting_purse). Change a value here and both engines follow.
Run `python3 tools/check_rules.py` after adding or renaming a rule.
settled     decided in the design docs
assumed     a working value for something still open; the note says which question
alternative a candidate kept off by default (docs/alternatives.md); only the web
engine implements these, and the Python simulator refuses non-defaults

startingPurse.note: Money each player starts with. docs/economy.md

startingIncome.note: Starting position on the income track; Earn pays this. docs/economy.md

incomePerBuilding.note: Income gained per building placed. Raised from 1 to 2 after early simulation; back to 1 once resources, pearls and the bigger board pushed final income to 13 against a target of ~8. docs/economy.md, docs/simulation.md

displaySize.note: Face-up market cards. Market structure is open question 10; docs/cards.md

rounds.note: A cap on the rounds (turns per player), against stalls: the game normally ends by endOnMarket or endOnKeys. It was a fixed 25 rounds up to playtest-v1. docs/next-version.md section 6

endOnMarket.note: The game ends at the end of the round in which the market decks run out (coastal and inland, both tiers; cards still in the displays don't count). docs/next-version.md section 6

endOnKeys.note: The game ends at the end of the round in which every key tile is on the sea-linked network. docs/next-version.md section 6

marketClock.note: The market clock, at the end of each round: the oldest card in a display leaves the game and the display refills, so the market runs down even when nobody buys. "unbought": only in a display nobody bought from this round (the designer's middle ground, 2026-11-10); "always": every open display; "off": never. docs/cards.md

inlandDisplay.note: true: coastal and inland cards are separate market decks, and the inland cards form a second display (displaySize cards) when the inland opens; until then, once the coastal deck and display are empty there is nothing to buy. false: inland cards shuffle into the coastal deck at the milestone (playtest-v1). Each deck is tiered: coastal-2 under coastal, inland-2 under inland. docs/cards.md

ownHarbours.note: Each player is assigned a harbour at setup (spread along the coast, in seat order). Starting dig cards may only start at your own harbour's mouth or share a corner with one of your own sea-linked canals; market dig cards may join anyone's network, as all digs did up to playtest-v1. docs/next-version.md section 5

endKeysShare.note: Raised to 1 on 2026-11-13 with the stage-3 rules, board and tides: at 0.5 games ran 30.6 rounds at four players and 26.5 at five, nearly all ending by keys; at 1, 35.7 and 36.3, the endings 3/13 and 6/6 keys/market. 0.85 asks as many villages as 1, and 0.8 as many as 0.7, at four and five players. The share of the key tiles endOnKeys counts (endKeysBand) that must be on the network for the game to end, rounded up: 1 is all of them, 0.5 half. With all five highland villages at four players the ending fired in 1 game of 12 (2.6 linked at the end on average); with half, in 4 of 12. docs/simulation.md

siteTokens.value: Spring=+1I:3:coast/inland; Ruins=+3M:4:coast; Ruins=2T:3:inland; Old lock=+1D:2:inland; Hoard=+1P:2:inland/highland
siteTokens.note: Site tokens (stage 2): name=effect:copies:bands. Dealt face up at random to the map's token sites (hexes.csv `token`) at setup, each to a site in one of its bands; the first building on a site takes its token, resolved like part of the card that built it. Blank: no tokens. docs/brainstorm-stage-2-3.md 3.4

hauling.note: How resources reach a build (stage 2, docs/next-version.md section 2). "tolls": sources never run out; clay is free from any shore hex, wood and stone cost extractionFee to the camp's or quarry's owner (free from your own); each comes the cheapest way over linked canals, paying tollPerCanal to the owner of every canal of someone else's (yours are free), and stone also stoneBankToll a canal to the bank, yours included. No import market. "cubes": stage 1 (docs/resources.md): cubes on extractors and an import market, hauled at haulPerEdge

tollPerCanal.note: Under hauling "tolls": what a haul pays the owner of each canal of someone else's it uses

stoneBankToll.note: Under hauling "tolls": stone is dearer to haul, paying this much more a canal to the bank, on your own canals too

tollMode.note: "edge": a toll for every canal of someone else's on the route (the designer's rule); "owner": one toll per other player whose canals the route uses, however many (quicker to count at the table; brainstorm-stage-2-3.md 8.1)

harbourDraft.note: Under ownHarbours: before the first turn, players choose their harbours in reverse seat order (the last seat first), instead of being assigned them. brainstorm-stage-3.md 6.5

harbourPremium.note: Under harbourDraft: a deep harbour (at least two canals nearer the inland than the median harbour) costs this much of its player's starting money. brainstorm-stage-3.md 6.5

reachBands.note: Reach points for an opened hex by band: coast, inland, highland (terrain.csv `band`). 1,2,3 made the Reach lane carry the merchant bot (90% of its points, the best mean); 1,1,2 tones it down (docs/simulation.md). Blank: every hex scores vpPerReach, as up to stage 1. docs/next-version.md section 3

highlandNeedsBought.note: Starting dig cards may not dig a border touching the highland: only bought dig cards reach it. docs/brainstorm-stage-2-3.md 3.3

endKeysBand.note: Which key tiles endOnKeys counts: "highland" (only the highland villages) or blank (all of them). On the deep map the inland villages are linked long before the far ones. docs/brainstorm-stage-2-3.md 3.6

cardWeights.note: How much each card counts toward its colour's multiplier, by deck (coastal-2 counts as coastal): starting cards don't count, so trashing them costs no points. Was 1 for every card up to playtest-v1. docs/scoring.md

vpPerBuilding.note: Building score per building. Calibration table in docs/scoring.md

vpPerKey.note: Key score per key token. Raised from 4 after simulation; docs/simulation.md

vpPerReach.note: Reach score per opened hex. Was 2 for a while: simulation agents that dug poorly for Reach made the lane look weak; with Reach-aware digging, 1 balances. docs/scoring.md, docs/simulation.md

handSizeCap.note: Maximum hand size after +1S. Open question 11

buildNeedsNetwork.note: A building may only go on a hex that is on the canal network. docs/map-and-network.md

inlandMilestone.note: What opens the inland: "canals": inlandMilestonePerPlayer x players (rounded down) sea-linked canals bordering inland hexes, anyone's; "keys": that many key tiles on the network. Until then no canal may have inland on both sides, nothing is built inland, and the inland cards stay out of the market. "open": the first opened inland hex (the earlier rule); "none": open from the start. docs/map-and-network.md, open question 10

milestoneReward.note: First-mover reward (docs/source-notes.md): the player whose dig reaches the inland milestone takes this, resolved like a discovery: +1C is one extra buy that turn, just as the inland cards arrive. It was +3M, which mostly went to digger and tipped the field. A notation code; blank for none. docs/map-and-network.md

inlandMilestonePerPlayer.note: The inlandMilestone threshold per player, rounded down: 3 at two players, 4 at three, 6 at four, 7 at five. Per player because fewer players dig fewer canals; 6 at four players opens the inland around round 14 of 25. docs/simulation.md

materials.note: Resources as Brass-style cubes on the board (docs/resources.md): extractors put cubes on their hex, building types need resources, and each comes from the cheapest connected source or the import market, paying haul along linked canals plus a price. false: no resources, a build pays only its site. Open question 38

haulPerEdge.note: Money per canal edge to haul a cube from its source (extractor, harbour or hub) to the building site. Open question 38

marketTrack.note: The import market for each resource: cube prices, cheapest sold first, so the price rises as the market empties. Open question 38; docs/resources.md

marketEmptyPrice.note: The price of an import cube once that resource's market is empty: the market never runs dry, it just gets dear. Open question 38

extractionFee.note: Paid to an extractor's owner per cube taken from it, and to a Transport hub's owner per import through it; free from your own. Discounts never reduce it. Open question 38

buildingTypes.note: Choose a building type when you build, from board/buildings.csv (nine types). false: every building is the plain one, and any building on a forest or mountain is its camp. Open question 39; docs/buildings.md

pearls.note: A bonus for keeping cards (docs/core-loop.md): end a turn without having discarded and take a pearl. Pearls are spent on your turn from a small menu: pearlMoney money, a redraw, or (pearlActionCost pearls) one more action of the played card's kind. Open question 40

pearlEarning.note: "track": at the end of your turn, move your pearl marker one space per card still in your hand (not played or discarded); when it reaches the threshold, take a pearl and reset it. "noDiscard": the earlier rule, a pearl for ending a turn without discarding. docs/core-loop.md, open question 40

pearlThreshold.note: Spaces on the pearl track for a pearl, before the additions below. Aim: 6-7 pearls in a whole game. docs/core-loop.md

pearlUsedDivisor.note: The threshold rises by the pearls you have used this game divided by this, rounded down. 0: off

pearlStoredStep.note: The threshold rises by this for each pearl you are holding: spend regularly, or hoard and earn slower

pearlHandStep.note: The threshold rises by this for each card of hand size above the starting hand (a bigger hand keeps more)

pearlCap.note: Most pearls a player may hold. Was 3 when a pearl came every turn without discards. Open question 40

pearlMoney.note: Money for one pearl. Open question 40

pearlActionCost.note: Pearls for one more dig, build or buy (the played card's kind), at full cost. Open question 40

techBoard.note: The technology board (board/tech.csv), each player's honeycomb of building tokens: every building comes from it, from a slot next to an open one. "income": tokens, adjacency, the leap and +1 income under each inner slot only (buildings otherwise give none); "level1": the six inner slots' technologies too; "level2": the outer ones; "full": capstones; "off": buildings.csv supply and incomePerBuilding. brainstorm-stage-3.md 5.9

techLeapCost.note: Pearls to take a token from a slot not next to an open one (the leap). -1: no leaping.

tides.note: Three tides: the inland milestone sends the undrawn coastal tier-1 cards out of the game; the first highland village on the network (or the coastal deck running out) opens the highland to starting cards and sends the undrawn inland tier-1 cards out. brainstorm-stage-3.md 10.2

tideReward.note: What the player who turns the third tide by linking a highland village takes (the second tide comes with the milestone, which has milestoneReward).

multiplierSteps.note: Each colour's multiplier in steps: "count:multiplier" pairs, the highest count reached applies (0 gives x1, 1-3 x2, 4-6 x3, 7-9 x4, 10 or more x5). Blank: the weighted count itself (up to multiplierCap). brainstorm-stage-3.md 6.2

deckSizes.note: Market cards per deck at 2/3/4/5 players. Copies are cut, never designs, Earn first, then the design with the most copies. Blank: every copy at every count. brainstorm-stage-3.md 7.1

buyOnTopCost.note: Pay this much more to put a bought card on top of your draw pile (drawn at the end of the turn) instead of on your discard pile. -1: not allowed. brainstorm-stage-3.md 6.8

forageOne.note: Instead of playing a card, discard one face down for this much money; the turn ends with no pearl track progress. 0: not allowed. brainstorm-stage-3.md 6.3

forageHand.note: Or discard your whole hand for this much money; the turn ends with no pearl track progress. 0: not allowed.

multiplierCap.note: Cap on each colour-count multiplier; 0 is uncapped. Open question 9

incomeMode.note: "earn": Earn pays your income (settled). "round": passive income each round, rejected in docs/economy.md

connectionRequired.note: A new canal must extend the sea-connected network, like a road in Catan: start at a harbour mouth, or share a corner with a canal already linked to the sea (anyone's). false: dig anywhere, and a stranded ditch counts once something links it

endOnCrossing.note: The first completed crossing ends the game after that round

autoKeyTiles.note: Place this many random key tiles if the map has none
